entries.title: AI Intelligence Barrels: Price Wars & Financial Value #shorts
entries.summary: A short claims wildly different AI "intelligence" pricing across providers (OpenAI ~$26, Anthropic ~$56, versus roughly $1-$1.50 for Grok/Meta/Google and ~$0.50 for Chinese models), framing this gap as inevitable price rationalization. The figures carry no units or sourcing, so treat this as an unverified illustrative claim rather than confirmed pricing data.

entries.title: Why I NEVER Use /compact in Claude Code #claudecode #ai #shorts
entries.summary: A Claude Code short argues against relying on /compact, claiming it can quietly discard context you still need, and recommends /clear plus a faster context-reset workflow instead. The actual workflow is only shared with commenters, not shown publicly.

entries.title: Nobody Should Be Paying An Agency For This Anymore
entries.summary: Meta's official Facebook Ads connector for Claude can now build a full paused ad campaign from chat — objective, targeting, placements, and ad copy variants — while checking Pixel/Conversions API setup and recommending which ad sets to scale or kill. The video frames this as replacing agency work billed at 10-20% of ad spend.

entries.title: AI agent for jobs #chatgpt #aiagent #claude
entries.summary: A short teases an "AI agent for jobs" without naming the tool or showing how it actually applies to roles, leaving viewers (and commenters) unsure what it does or costs. No specific product or method is demonstrated.

entries.title: What happens when you ask Claude to rewrite your resume?
entries.summary: A short shows Claude being asked to rewrite a resume, illustrating the use case without detailing the prompt or method used. A commenter warns that AI resume rewrites can fabricate details (e.g. inventing a college major), a caution worth keeping in mind for this workflow.

entries.title: I Made ChatGPT Sell My Stuff And Negotiate For Me 🤯 #shorts  #ai #technology #aitutorial
entries.summary: A creator chains four ChatGPT prompts into a resale pipeline: identify and price items from photos, write a marketplace listing, have ChatGPT's browser agent post it to Facebook Marketplace, then run a recurring scheduled task that checks for buyers every 24 hours and negotiates on your behalf.

entries.title: The AI Engineer Move Most People Skip
entries.summary: A short argues the AI-engineer move most people skip is using tools like Cursor or Claude Code to build your own skills and agents, which teaches how these systems behave, plus preparing for interviews that mix LeetCode, system design, and AI-specific domain questions.

entries.title: AI stack for July 2026
entries.summary: A creator teases his current "AI stack for July 2026" with no on-screen detail beyond the title; commenters speculate about tools like Apex and Higgsfield, but none of that is confirmed by the creator, so no specific product can be verified from this video alone.
